definitions.explanation: having a dark, depressing, or cheerless quality

examples.japanese: {陰気|いんき}な{天気|てんき}が{続|つづ}く。
この{部屋|へや}は{陰気|いんき}な{雰囲気|ふんいき}がある。
examples.english: This room has a dreary atmosphere.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{陰気|いんき}な{顔|かお}をして{黙|だま}っていた。
examples.english: He sat silently with a gloomy expression.

notes:
{陰気|いんき} is a na-adjective describing a dark, gloomy, or depressing quality in people, places, weather, or atmosphere.

ETYMOLOGY:
{陰|いん} (yin, shadow, negative) + {気|き} (spirit, atmosphere). Rooted in the {陰陽|いんよう} (yin-yang) concept.

FORMS:
- Na-adjective: {陰気|いんき}な{雰囲気|ふんいき} (gloomy atmosphere)
- Adverbial: {陰気|いんき}に{黙|だま}り{込|こ}む (sit in gloomy silence)

CAN DESCRIBE:
- {天気|てんき}: weather (dreary, overcast)
- {雰囲気|ふんいき}: atmosphere (depressing)
- {性格|せいかく}: personality (gloomy, somber)
- {場所|ばしょ}: places (dark, cheerless)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {陽気|ようき}: cheerful, lively, bright — the direct opposite
- {暗|くら}い: dark (more general, also literal darkness)
- {憂鬱|ゆううつ}: depressed, melancholy (focuses on internal feelings)
- じめじめ: damp and gloomy (onomatopoeia, physical sensation)
